headline: Vice President Gibran's resignation and a record-low rupiah (JISDOR 18,241) cheapen the 2–5Y by 4–7bp while the 10Y rises only 1.6bp to 7.69%; the JCI's 2.7% jump lifts the daily flow signal to −0.67, still in sell-off
summary: PHEI's IGSYC sold off from the front and belly: the 1Y rose 4.8bp to 6.776%, the 2Y 6.7bp to 7.020%, the 3Y 6.5bp to 7.188% and the 5Y 4.4bp to 7.453%, while the 10Y added only 1.6bp to 7.689% and 15–30Y 1.2bp, so the curve bear-flattened (2s5s 43.3bp from 45.6bp, 5s10s 23.6bp from 26.4bp). The 10Y is still 1.4bp lower on the week but 6.2bp higher this month and in the 97th percentile of the past year. Benchmark FR0109 lost 11.3bp to 7.439% and is now 6.2bp cheap to the curve, while FR0108 (7.616%) stays 6.5bp rich. The fitted PBS curve sits 1.9bp over IGSYC at 2Y and 1.1bp through at 5Y, the retail fit is 10.1bp rich at 5Y, and AAA 3Y rose 6.1bp to 7.68%, 49.2bp over, moving with the government curve again.
drivers: Rupiah at a record low pushed the belly

JISDOR rose 0.48% to 18,241 and spot closed at 18,239, both record weak, as the dollar index hit its highest since March 2025 on December Fed-hike pricing (BI's explanation) and the Vice President's exit added domestic risk. The 2–5Y took the hit (+4.4 to +6.7bp) and FR0109 fell 11.3bp; who sold is not published, and a dealer-led markdown of the belly rather than outright foreign selling is my hypothesis.
Gibran resigned; stocks rallied, bonds did not

Gibran handed his resignation to the MPR and the President on Thursday; the MPR has 60 days to install a replacement. The JCI jumped 2.66% to 5,250.90, closing at its high, with foreigners net buying Rp443.5bn across the market (IDX data via Kontan), so equities read the exit as an end to the impeachment fight, while the rupiah and short bonds priced the vacancy.
No US cash session overnight; Tuesday's shock still unpaid

US cash Treasuries were shut for Veterans Day, so there was no New York close since the last PHEI close and Treasuries explain none of the 10Y's +1.6bp at the 1-year daily beta of 0.33. Tuesday's 10bp jump implied about +3.3bp that INDOGBs never priced; today's rise may be partial catch-up, and cash reopened Thursday about 2bp higher near 5.00%. The INDOGB − UST spread is 271bp (92nd percentile of 52 weeks), a nominal pick-up before currency risk.
MSCI review was a non-event for bonds

MSCI dropped BRPT and BRMS from its Standard index and seven names from Small Cap, effective after the Nov 30 close; brokers estimate about Rp1–1.2tn of passive outflow, small against the market, and the Standalone decision is still due by June 2027. Bloomberg-compiled data show $174m of foreign money into INDOGBs so far in November, but a month's inflows do not rule out selling later in the month.
data: BRPT, BRMS out of Standard; 7 out of Small Cap (f BRPT, BRMS deletions expected; p index freeze)
In line; est. Rp1–1.2tn passive outflow on Nov 30. Standalone risk unchanged.
US 10Y to ~5% and a December Fed hike fully priced; the dollar's rally is now the rupiah's main headwind.
Bids Rp79.71tn (p Rp31.09tn); awarded Rp35tn vs Rp30tn target; FR0110 7.44%, FR0111 7.68%
Strong demand at higher yields; foreign bids 22.6% of the book. FR0109 at 7.44% now trades at FR0110's auction yield.
Soft consumption argues against hikes for growth reasons.
Firmer sentiment; no change to the BI call.
My read, not a BI commitment: BI has room to smooth the rupiah, but 18,200 is already broken.
A beat: no growth case for an early cut.
view: The day says the rupiah, not Treasuries or MSCI, is setting the price of short INDOGBs: with JISDOR through 18,200 the market is starting to price a BI response, and that is why the 2–5Y cheapened while the 10Y barely moved. The daily Bond Flow Signal rose to −0.67 from −0.77 as the JCI's rally eased its part (z −1.29), but the 10Y trend (z +1.82, +51.9bp over 20 sessions) and the rupiah (z +0.57, +1.70%) keep it in sell-off, with only the 271bp Treasury spread, 27.3bp above its 130-day average (z +1.01), bond-bullish. On the daily build the Oct 7 episode ended Nov 6 with the 10Y 51.0bp higher, and a new sell-off episode opened Nov 10 (+0.5bp after three sessions). Since June 2022 the daily signal scores a Sharpe of 0.74 outright and 0.87 hedged against Treasuries, but sell-off calls were right only 51% of the time over the next 20 sessions (rally calls 58%; hedged 62% and 51%); the weekly build scores 0.42 and 0.57, and the US-trend variants reach 0.73 and 0.78 on the weekly build but were chosen after the fact and are not live; all are in-sample back-tests. Over four weeks Treasuries explain only +2.7bp of the 10Y's +50.9bp (weekly beta −0.22), leaving +48.2bp that the US move does not explain. I stay neutral on the 10Y in a 7.55–7.80% range for the next two weeks: the underweight needs a close above 7.75% as well as the signal below −0.5. On the curve, the belly is finally cheapening toward my FR0109 entry (7.60–7.70%), and I would rather buy 5Y there after BI (Nov 17–18) than add 1–2Y.

buckets.name: Front end 1–2Y vs BI-Rate
buckets.why: The IGSYC 1Y rose 4.8bp to 6.776%, 102.6bp over the 5.75% BI-Rate (18th percentile of 11 stored days, average 109.5bp), back above my 6.75% no-chase line after one day below it; the 2Y rose 6.7bp to 7.020%. The 3M (0.25Y) is 6.30% and the 1M 6.20%, 120bp over the 5.00% deposit facility. The 7.10% add level was not reached (32bp away).
buckets.call: Neutral. Add 1–2Y only at 1Y 7.10% or after a BI hike that steadies JISDOR; a hike on Nov 18 would hit this bucket first.

buckets.name: Belly 5Y (FR0109 / PBS040)
buckets.why: The IGSYC 5Y rose 4.4bp to 7.453% (45th percentile of 11 stored days, average 7.494%), still 6.8bp lower this month; the 2s5s10s fly is 19.7bp (45th percentile, average 26.0bp). FR0109 fell 11.3bp to 7.439% and is 6.2bp cheap to the curve; PBS040 at 7.438% is 10.7bp cheap. The entry (FR0109 7.60–7.70%) is 16bp away and not filled.
buckets.call: Buy FR0109 at 7.60–7.70% after a BI hike or with JISDOR back below 18,000; target 7.35%, stop 7.95%.

buckets.name: 10Y outright
buckets.why: The IGSYC 10Y rose 1.6bp to 7.689%, 97th percentile of the past year (173 days, average 6.81%) and 3.5bp under the 7.724% high of Nov 4. The signal is −0.67, but the underweight rule also needs a 10Y close above 7.75%, so it is not triggered. FR0108 at 7.616% is 6.5bp rich; FR0111 cleared at 7.68% at Tuesday's auction.
buckets.call: Neutral, range 7.55–7.80%. Underweight if the signal stays below −0.5 and the 10Y closes above 7.75%; tactical long only above 7.85% (stop 8.05%) or once the signal is above 0 with JISDOR below 18,000.

buckets.name: 10s20s curve (FR0108 vs FR0107)
buckets.why: IGSYC 10s20s is 2.2bp (73rd percentile of 11 stored days, average 1.3bp, range 0.1–2.9bp); the range is tiny. The benchmark spread FR0107 − FR0108 widened to 5.2bp from 2.9bp, 10.2bp away from the −5bp re-entry. FR0113 (2047) was not awarded on Tuesday, so 20Y supply is deferred, not cancelled.
buckets.call: Wait. Re-enter the FR0108/FR0107 steepener duration-weighted at −5bp or lower, target +5bp, stop −12bp.

buckets.name: PBS sukuk vs FR
buckets.stance: FR over PBS034 at the long end
buckets.why: The fitted PBS 5Y is 1.1bp through IGSYC (50th percentile of ten stored days, average −1.9bp), the 2Y 1.9bp over and the 10Y 3.0bp through; the fit rests on four series (level −5.2bp, slope 11.2bp), so confidence is limited. PBS034 rose 1.5bp to 7.607% and is 6.5bp rich, PBS040 10.7bp cheap. The switch-back condition (PBS034 5bp cheap) is not met; the position stays open.
buckets.call: Hold FR over PBS034; switch back once PBS034 is 5bp cheap to IGSYC. PBS040 at ~11bp cheap suits buy-and-hold accounts.

buckets.name: Corporate credit (AAA 3Y)
buckets.why: PHEI's AAA 3Y rose 6.1bp to 7.680%, 49.2bp over IGSYC (10th percentile of ten stored days, average 50.6bp). AA is 87.3bp over, A 154.2bp, and BBB 231.4bp over AA (10th percentile, average 242.8bp): the curves again tracked IGSYC. PEFINDO reports corporate issuance down 12.75% to September as funding costs rose. Ten days is a thin base; the add level (AAA 3Y past 70bp) was not reached.
buckets.call: Hold AAA/AA; add only if AAA 3Y widens past 70bp. Avoid BBB until the rupiah and politics settle.

buckets.name: Retail SBN 5Y (ORI/SR)
buckets.why: The fitted retail curve is 10.1bp through IGSYC at 5Y, the least rich of ten stored days (average −13.8bp), and 11.1bp over at 2Y; the 22-series fit has an 80bp slope, so part of this is fit artefact. Secondary spreads run from 63bp rich (SR022T3) to 39bp cheap (ORI027T3); ORI026T6 is 7.571%, 29bp over. ST017 (open to Dec 2) floors at 6.95% (2Y) and 7.05% (4Y), now below the IGSYC 2Y (7.02%).
buckets.call: For new money, FR0109 or PBS040 give daily liquidity; ST017 suits hold-to-maturity buyers who want BI-hike upside. Buy secondary retail only at the cheap end (ORI026T6, ~29bp over).

watch: Next: US PPI (Fri Nov 13), IDX's removal of high-concentration stocks from the JCI (from Fri Nov 13), Indonesia's October trade balance (mid-November), the MPR's process to fill the vice presidency (60 days), BI's board meeting (Nov 17–18), MSCI changes effective after the Nov 30 close and the ST017 book closing Dec 2; a 10Y close above 7.75% would trigger the underweight, while JISDOR back below 18,000 would push a BI hike out.
